labels.zh-CN: 急慢比（28 天平均为 0 时无值）
labels.en: Acute:chronic ratio (no value when the 28-day average is zero)

details.formulaDescription: Both loads must use the same session-load method, typically duration in minutes multiplied by a 1-10 perceived-exertion score and summed over the period. When chronicLoad > 0, acuteChronicRatio = acuteLoad / chronicLoad rounded to two decimals, and weeklyRampPercent = (acuteLoad - chronicLoad) / chronicLoad × 100 rounded to one decimal. Bands use the rounded ratio: below 0.8 low, 0.8 to 1.3 inclusive typical, above 1.3 up to 1.5 elevated, above 1.5 spike. When chronicLoad is 0 the ratio and ramp are undefined and the band is unknown. WeeklyTrainingMinutes, sessionsPerWeek and averageRpe are validation and context inputs; they do not alter the ratio.
assumptions: Acute and chronic load use the same session-load formula; mixing methods makes the ratio meaningless.
The 0.8, 1.3 and 1.5 thresholds are an experience-based heuristic; the evidence linking training load to injury is conflicting.
The 28-day average is treated as a stable reference even though training patterns change week to week.
A low ratio may reflect a planned recovery week or incomplete records rather than undertraining.
The tool does not diagnose overtraining syndrome; persistent fatigue and performance decline need clinical assessment.
details.rounding: Ratio to two decimal places; weekly ramp percent to one decimal place; the band is assigned from the rounded ratio, so no further tolerance is applied; the note is text and is not rounded.
